verdict.rationale: Blaxel documents the whole loop for agents. Its agent skill lets an agent create sandboxes from prompts. The SDK and each sandbox's built-in MCP server let the agent run processes, read files and retrieve output logs. Teardown is covered by expiration policies that auto-delete sandboxes and by archive/shutdown, and API keys allow non-interactive SDK/CLI access. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented agent-initiated sandbox delete call (teardown evidence covers auto-expiration and archive only), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the unattended end-to-end flow.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote: Install the Blaxel skill to give your agent the ability to deploy AI agents, create sandboxes for code execution
Every Blaxel sandbox exposes a built-in MCP server so agents can operate the sandbox using tool calls for files, processes, ports, and previews.
Run shell commands, retrieve process information, and control process execution.
Retrieve process output logs from sandboxes in batch or real-time streaming mode
Read, write, list, and delete files inside a Blaxel sandbox using a simple file system interface from the SDK, MCP server, or REST API.
Configure expiration policies to automatically delete Blaxel sandboxes after inactivity, a TTL, or other conditions
API keys can be used in the Blaxel APIs, CLI and SDK.
